title: Fāṭima, daughter of Aḥmad of Burtuqāl, bears Aḥmad ibn Yūsuf of the dīwān a son, Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī

Abū al-Faḍl, sultan of Fās since 1381 and the Emperor's ally in the War of Jillīqiya, dies of pneumonia at fifty-seven. His son Abū Ḥammū had died in 1410, and the throne passes to his grandson Yaḥyā, fifteen

data.successor: Yaḥyā, born 14 July 1401, son of Abū Ḥammū (died 14 September 1410, a hunting accident); in his own name from 14 July 1417

title: The Ottomans make a great peace in Anatolia and on the Danube: Sivas and the lands of Eretna, Amasya and the Pontic hills, the Dobruja from Bulgaria and Reni from Wallachia, thirty-one towns in all

data.note: counted from the towns that changed hands that day (the world beyond the realm)

title: Yaḥyā of Fās, great-grandson of Yūsuf I through Jadīla, comes of age and rules in his own name. Fās stays the Emperor's ally
Saʿd ibn Yūsuf, the Emperor's nephew, raised at his court since the age of four, takes Umm al-Fatḥ's empty seat in the dīwān, integrating the new lands
